scope: Standalone default HttpExchange.onAbort and common AbortListeners contracts only. Built-in transport detection and core request lifetime integration remain separate obligations.
coverage: The new hook is reflected as a default void method. A pre-existing RecordingExchange inherits it without an override and remains usable. Null listeners fail, and the default remains a no-op on successful finish and legacy abort.
Each registration receives one notification, including duplicate Runnable registrations, repeated abort, and listeners registered after abort. Initial and terminal isAborted state are asserted.
Both RuntimeException and Error from listeners do not stop later callbacks; a throwing late callback also does not prevent the next late listener.
Reentrant abort and listener registration do not duplicate callbacks.
A listener joins a different thread that registers another callback. The explicit joined flag and callback count reject implementations that hold the registry lock while invoking user code.
Twenty rounds race eight registration workers covering400 distinct registrations with repeated abort. Every registration has an independent exactly-once counter and bounded Future waits.
Null listener rejection is asserted both before and after the terminal state.
The historical SPI inventory retains every prior signature and names only the intended additive hook alongside earlier approved additions.

red_evidence.inventory_failure: Expected onAbort addition is absent before implementation.

remaining_obligations: Actual built-in adapter registration and timeout/disconnect/write failure notification.
Core registration before user callbacks, synchronous abort during registration, recursion prevention, and request cleanup exactly once.
Normal built-in finish versus abort and WS/SSE regression checks after integration.
Actual Java8/API21 verification of the implemented default and helper.
loop_policy: PASS at round1 for this component scope. Stop now; no round2 or round3.
